retrieved_synopses: Voss waits in the sewers until you get the hammer. Then he's there with the dragon he rode in Act1 in humanoid form. If you show him the hammer then, he rewards you with a Silver Sword and then leaves to meet you in endgame.He will still be in endgame even if you didn't do this step, but you just would have missed on the Silver Sword.

The exchange happens at the late‑game “point of no return” just before the final approach to the Netherbrain. Off‑screen the party has just stolen or otherwise acquired a key item called the Hammer from Raphael’s lair, and Kith’rak Voss expects you to bring it to him beneath the city — he promises reward and offers the traditional githyanki silver sword as a token. Whether Voss is an ally or a hostile accuser depends on earlier choices around Prince Orpheus (alive, dead, or transformed) and other late‑game decisions (the Netherstones/tadpole), so companions and other voices nearby warn against sharing or trusting him. This scene follows directly after the Voss/Raphael moment and reflects the high tension and fragile loyalties before the final confrontation.
After WithersChronicles, if the player made the deal with Raphael (the Orphic Hammer in exchange for the Crown of Karsus), Raphael shows up to report back on how that went.
The introduction dialog with Voss, where Raphael dismisses him to then talk to the player in private.

The player has burned their bridges. They attacked the Emperor, causing him to leave the Astral Prism as a foe, and they have no hammer to free Orpheus, as they need his protection against the influence of the Netherbrain. After a short pause to let the players feel the weight of their actions, Raphael appears before them, with a new deal: accept the hammer from Raphael, freeing Orpheus in exchange for giving him the Crown. At this point, the player has no other option except for a game over.
context: This takes place immediately after the late‑game confrontation with Raphael: off‑screen the party has just acquired (or stolen) the Orphic Hammer from Raphael’s lair and the player has come to meet Kith’rak Voss beneath the city. Voss had instructed you to bring the Hammer and promises a reward — the traditional githyanki silver sword — which he offers here if you show it. Companions nearby warn against sharing or trusting him, because whether Voss is an ally or a hostile accuser depends on earlier choices about Prince Orpheus and other late‑game decisions (Netherstones / tadpole). If you missed an earlier sewer step you could forfeit the Silver Sword, but Voss will still appear in the endgame regardless.
